clue.text: Teaspoon preference to hand. Oh for no trouble brewing like this!

annotation.answer: ONE FOR EACH PERSON AND ONE FOR THE POT

definitions.text: Teaspoon preference to hand. Oh for no trouble brewing like this!

indicators.note: brewing is stirring things up, so the words before it are churned into a fresh order

blocks.clueFragment: Teaspoon preference to hand. Oh for no
blocks.note: every letter of these seven words is used, punctuation ignored

explanation.surface: A tea-drinker states how many spoonfuls they like and hopes for a hitch-free pot.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the letters to rearrange and the definition: it describes the traditional rule for making a pot of tea. The answer runs across 1, 13 and 11.
explanation.definitionFit: The old British rule for measuring loose tea into a teapot: a spoonful per drinker plus an extra spoonful.

clue.text: Pharisee was just mendacious, not a twister

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the word that follows it
a twister bends things out of shape, so the remaining letters are wrenched into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: A Pharisee is accused of being merely a liar, though not a crooked one.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one A from MENDACIOUS and the nine letters left rearrange into NICODEMUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicodemus is the Pharisee in John's Gospel who visited Jesus by night; he is the example named here.

clue.text: Meal a Six Counties service sent up

indicators.note: in a down answer, sending something up means writing it from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
the Six Counties are Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI
the Royal Air Force, one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A meal is laid on by a military unit in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Ireland is made up of six counties, hence the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Farina is flour or fine meal ground from cereal grain, so meal is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Check puncture and bearing, then restonre the pressure

blocks.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
a flat is a punctured tyre
east, a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Motoring advice: inspect the puncture and the wheel bearing, then pump the tyre back up.
explanation.walkthrough: The source prints 'restonre', a typo for 'restore'.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflate something again is to bring back the air pressure it had lost.

clue.text: Bigot of the Right is caught in the act

indicators.note: something caught in something else is held inside it

blocks.note: R is the standard abbreviation for right
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A right-wing bigot is caught red-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: A racist is a particular kind of bigot, one prejudiced against people of other races.

clue.text: He's understood to have relations

blocks.note: first meaning: the radio word saying a message has been received and understood
second meaning: British slang for having sex with someone

explanation.surface: A man is said to have family connections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relations' looks like family, but the second meaning is sexual relations; the man's name in the answer also suits 'He'.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio operators say it to acknowledge a message received, and in British slang it is a crude verb for sex.

clue.text: Tradesperson: one dividing clergy and monarch

indicators.note: something dividing two things sits between them, splitting them apart

blocks.note: the cloth is a collective term for the clergy
Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tradesman comes between church and crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothier makes or sells cloth or clothes, so is a tradesman of a particular kind.

clue.text: when the students rise?

blocks.note: surface reading: the time undergraduates get out of bed
setter's reading: the National Union of Students written upward in a down entry

explanation.walkthrough: NUS is the National Union of Students; read upward, as a Down light is, it spells the first half of the answer, with UP saying which way. The question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunup is the time of morning when the sun rises, another word for dawn or sunrise.

clue.text: Bowled one eccentric, one rum

blocks.note: B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled
a, the indefinite article, means one
a card is an old word for an eccentric character
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cricket report: one batsman bowled, another rather odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' reads as odd, matching 'eccentric', but here it is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacardi is a well-known brand of white rum, so it is an example of the spirit.

clue.text: So the unions would ban Norman? That's criminal!

blocks.note: to black something is for a trade union to boycott it
Norman Mailer, the American novelist

explanation.surface: A wry comment that trade unions boycotting a man named Norman would be a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: Blacking was the British trade-union term for refusing to handle goods or work during a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who extorts money by threatening to reveal secrets commits a crime, so is a criminal.

clue.text: It's gross to confess one's over the hill

definitions.note: a jokey noun phrase: one who is no longer young

blocks.note: gr. is the abbreviation for gross, twelve dozen
to own up is to confess

explanation.surface: Someone admits, with distaste, to being past their prime.
explanation.definitionFit: An adult has left childhood behind, which the clue exaggerates playfully as being past one's prime.

clue.text: Add runs among the crew to rectify

indicators.note: something among a group sits in the middle of it

blocks.note: to put on is to add, as with weight or runs
a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A rowing or cricket coach adds running work to the crew's training to fix a fault.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct someone's mistake or misunderstanding is to set them straight, i.e. rectify matters.

clue.text: See 1
Hank employed from this wolly strand

indicators.note: from says the letters are drawn out of the words that come before it

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A hank of yarn is being used from a woollen thread.
explanation.walkthrough: The source prints 'wolly', a typo for 'woolly'. 'Hank' looks like a skein of wool, part of the definition, but it supplies only its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Kemp is the coarse, brittle hair or fibre mixed in among a fleece's finer wool.

clue.text: See 1
Weight displacing the cargo mark

indicators.note: displacing shifts things out of position, so these letters are moved around

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for the old German mark

explanation.surface: Shifting a ship's load moves its weight past the loading mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A hectogram is a metric unit of mass equal to a hundred grams, so it is a weight.

clue.text: Nodding off in the Cowes road? A thousand times no!

indicators.note: the letters that follow are placed in the middle of the stretch of water
multiplication in algebra is written by placing symbols side by side

blocks.note: the Solent is the strait off Cowes; roads are a sheltered anchorage
the Roman numeral for a thousand
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor nods off at anchor off the Isle of Wight and is roundly scolded.
explanation.walkthrough: Cowes is the yachting town on the Isle of Wight, facing the Solent strait off England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Somnolent means drowsy or sleepy, the state of someone whose head is nodding as sleep comes.

clue.text: The end of the pier show around this column

indicators.note: around means wrapping about something, holding it inside

blocks.note: taken as written
the last is the end

explanation.surface: A seaside end-of-the-pier variety show is staged around a supporting post.
explanation.walkthrough: An end-of-the-pier show is a traditional British seaside variety entertainment; the phrase must be split apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilaster is a flat rectangular column projecting slightly from a wall, so it is a kind of column.

clue.text: Lack money to enter the Order of Rechabites ...

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it

blocks.note: an absence is a lack
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone can't afford to join a temperance society.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rechabites of the Bible refused wine, and the Independent Order of Rechabites is a temperance society; what they order, and the order they belong to, is going without drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Refraining from alcohol is the vow the Rechabites take, so it is literally what their order commands.

clue.text: ... order a Rechabite initially might give to a Persian wine-lover

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the Order of Merit, a British honour
taken as written
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A teetotal society member might hand a Persian poet his wine, continuing the previous clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses link this clue to 17, but each clue is solved separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Omar Khayyam, the Persian poet of the Rubaiyat, celebrated wine in his verses, so he is a wine-lover.

clue.text: Ad libs are not in it!

definitions.text: Ad libs are not in it!

blocks.clueFragment: Ad libs are not in it!
blocks.note: surface reading: a remark about improvised lines

blocks.clueFragment: Ad libs are not in it
blocks.note: setter's reading: the written text actors learn, which by definition leaves out anything improvised

explanation.walkthrough: An ad lib is something spoken off the cuff, so it can never appear in the prepared words of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: The written text of a play or film contains only the planned lines, never those improvised on stage.

clue.text: 11 not 1,000 Hong Kong cups, alas, smashed

definitions.note: the answer to 11, one for the pot, read as a kind of tea

indicators.note: not tells us the following item is left out
smashed cups break into pieces that are put back together differently

blocks.note: K, for kilo, stands for a thousand
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sad tale of a thousand teacups broken in Hong Kong.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the K of KONG and the remaining fifteen letters rearrange. The definition is the cross-reference: the tea is the 'one for the pot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapsang souchong is a smoky Chinese black tea, one variety to spoon into a teapot.

clue.text: Olympic ultimatum has weight in China

indicators.note: has means the words before contain the answer within them

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An Olympic final demand carries weight in China, host of the Games.
explanation.definitionFit: A picul is a traditional East Asian unit of mass, roughly what one man can carry on a shoulder pole.

clue.text: One hand in glove in France with Ulysses

indicators.note: in places the preceding item inside what follows

blocks.note: gant is French for glove
right, one of the two hands, abbreviated R

explanation.surface: A French glove story: a hand slipped inside, in company with a hero named Ulysses.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulysses S. Grant was the Union general and later US president.
explanation.definitionFit: Grant's first name was Ulysses, so the forename stands for the man here.

clue.text: Educated woman gets out of bed for such cheese

indicators.note: here read as getting outside something, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: from Educating Rita, Willy Russell's play and film
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A learned lady rises from bed to fetch some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets out of bed' reads as rising, but cryptically the woman goes around the outside of the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft white Italian cheese made from whey, so 'such cheese' is an example.

clue.text: Dress with the end let out

indicators.note: with is read as 'holding within', so one piece carries the other inside

blocks.note: to rent a room is to let it out
an aim is an end or goal

explanation.surface: A dressmaker lets out a gown's hem to lengthen it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let out' sounds like dressmaking, matching the surface, but it is a landlord's renting.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for clothing, so it means dress in the general sense.

clue.text: "Bit of a Bloomer Arising" (Lawrence Harris)

indicators.note: arising usually signals a down entry going up, here used for a backward reading

blocks.note: T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia
Rolf Harris, the Australian entertainer

explanation.surface: A spoof book title with its author, like the jokey 'books' in schoolboy humour.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue mimics a joke title and author pair; the two famous names are the wordplay, read backwards together.
explanation.definitionFit: A floret is one of the small flowers making up a composite bloom, so it is part of a flower.

clue.text: Genetically modify a mongrel without a sign of energy

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so it wraps around what follows

blocks.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog
taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Instructions to genetically alter a mongrel without giving it any vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutate is to change in form, particularly by an alteration in the genes.
